web_evidence.title: The Children of Húrin Excerpt
web_evidence.note: Publisher-authorized excerpt begins with Túrin aged seventeen and externally recounts his grief, Morgoth's growing power, and Thingol's protection. Establishes third-person interior narration.

web_evidence.title: The Children of Hurin — J. R. R. Tolkien
web_evidence.note: Substantial Chapter One excerpt surveys several family members, their dispositions and histories, then redirects the tale to Húrin and Huor. Corroborates an external narrator at the opening.

web_evidence.title: Nostalgia Review: Children of Hurin
web_evidence.note: Review explicitly describes the book's narrative style as third person, corroborating the primary excerpts.

web_evidence.title: UNESP dissertation on Tolkien's tragic hero
web_evidence.note: Page 93 contextualizes q01325 as Túrin's rebuke of the outlaws after their treatment of Beleg. Resolves its first-person plural as dialogue.

web_evidence.title: Document 55175 — The Children of Húrin transcription
web_evidence.note: Lower-provenance transcription supplies several corroborating contexts: q01314 is Túrin's speech, q01321 Asgon's, q01349 Mablung's, and q01331/q01347 Melian's advice. Used for local attribution alongside authorized prose.

web_evidence.title: Beleg Strongbow
web_evidence.note: Forum quotation explicitly attributes q01319 to Beleg; ancillary attribution evidence, not independent proof of the 2007 book's structure.

search_log: Searched The Children of Hurin Tolkien excerpt chapter; found and opened BookBrowse's authorized interior excerpt and AbeBooks' opening excerpt.
Searched the title with narrator third person; opened JC Murray's explicit third-person review. Audiobook-narrator results were not treated as narrative-person evidence.
Searched exact phrases from q01314, q01319, q01321, q01325 and q01349 to resolve apparent first-person narration.
Opened the UNESP dissertation and inspected its discussion of Túrin addressing the outlaws.
Opened the ABCdocz transcription and located speech contexts for the ambiguous quotations, including Melian's advice and Mablung's lament.
Opened Korpua's Constructive Mythopoetics dissertation; its parallel Mablung quotation cites a 1999 Tolkien text, so it was not treated as direct evidence for the 2007 edition.
The Hopkins and Company interior-excerpt result failed to open and was not used as evidence.
person_note: The controlling narrator recounts the characters externally, including their motives and emotions. Diagnostic Goodreads passages agree with the authorized interior excerpt, the opening, and an explicit whole-book review. Apparent first-person event quotations resolve into character dialogue; Christopher Tolkien's first-person editorial introduction is paratext. These do not establish alternating narration. Existing upstream classifications remain unchanged, with possible speech-versus-event issues noted. The main limitation is that authorized web coverage is excerpt-based rather than a complete edition; no credible contrary narrative structure emerged.
